title: Multiplexed Trace Courier & ID Translation for gRPC/HTTP2 Streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation:
gRPC over HTTP/2 frequently multiplexes many logical streams over a single connection. In high-throughput Redwood services we observe trace context loss or collision when streams are hijacked by proxies, when metadata size grows, or when language SDKs eagerly inline large propagation blobs into headers. This ticket proposes a small-footprint, backpressure-safe carrier pattern ("MuxCourier") plus an ID translation layer to reliably preserve and stitch request traces across multiplexed streams and streaming RPCs without inflating headers or changing existing W3C-compatible upstream formats.

Solution sketch:
- Introduce a lightweight short-courier header (X-Redwood-Courier: <sid>) used for intra-cluster multiplexed hops. The sid is a 64-bit stable short id (base62) mapped locally to the full trace envelope in an in-process KV with TTL and bounded memory.
- SDK/middleware behavior: on outgoing stream creation, if full trace envelope already present, emit sid only and write full envelope to local KV; on inbound requests carrying sid, lookup local KV and rehydrate full tracing context into the request's context.
- For cross-host hops (eg. external clients or proxies that don't speak sid), fall back to existing traceparent/tracestate headers. Gate translation rules: sid preferred for same-connection path; full envelope preferred for cross-connection.
- Implement eviction and collision handling: sid collisions logged and resolved by generating new sid and emitting update control span to aid debugging. Use monotonic SID generation per-process to reduce collision window.
- Sampling hints: propagate a compact sampling byte alongside sid (X-Redwood-S) so downstream samplers can decide without full envelope.
- Safety: ensure protected path for streaming backpressure — lookups are async-safe and non-blocking; on lookup miss we allow a trace-less but gracefully degraded request rather than block the stream.
- Compatibility: SDK adapters for Node, Python, and Java; middleware for Envoy filter and internal edge proxy.

Non-goals: replacing W3C headers globally, storing any PII in sid mapping, or cross-process shared state beyond short-lived in-process mapping.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (node/python/java) expose MuxCourier and default to 'sid-first' for same-connection flows
End-to-end test: streaming gRPC request that creates 1000 multiplexed logical streams preserves parent trace id for >= 99.95% of streams
Performance: additional per-request p99 latency overhead < 0.3ms in microbenchmarks
Memory: per-sid mapping average < 256 bytes and TTL eviction prevents unbounded growth
Console: spans re-attach in Trace Explorer and a dashboard shows sid-to-trace mappings for debugging
Fallback: when sid is unknown, system emits diagnostic metric redwood.trace.sid.lookup_miss and continues without blocking the stream

progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with SDK, runtime, and proxies. Agreed on sid-first preference and fallback rules (Aisha, Marco, Riley).
2025-02-18: PoC Node SDK implementation (local sid map + header emitter) validated on internal chat service; lost-context rate reduced from 0.6% to 0.02% under synthetic load.
2025-02-21: Perf microbenchmark showing 0.12ms median overhead; memory profile shows ~180B per mapping for simple trace envelope encoding.
2025-02-26: Design reviewed by infra/security; request to add explicit sampling hint header and TTL hard limit (default 60s).
2025-03-01: Envoy filter prototype implemented; initial integration tests pass. Opened PR for Node SDK: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/2189.

2025-03-03: Found a blocker: rare sid collision when processes restarted with same monotonic seed during fast redeploys. Agreed mitigation: append 8-bit random nonce and emit collision metric; follow-up ticket created for persistent authoritative mapping across hot restarts.
comments: Riley Thompson (runtime): We need to ensure the lookup path is lock-free for Node worker threads. Consider using a concurrent circular buffer for eviction.
Sana Kaur (security): Confirmed no PII is stored; add audit log entry when full envelope is rehydrated from local mapping.
Marco Chen (assignee): Will prototype 8-bit nonce to reduce collision window; aiming for patch by 2025-03-05.
Design review note: prefer emitting sid-only for same-connection requests to keep header sizes small; but allow opt-out via SDK config for debugging.
